AssetType.description: What kind of media an asset holds (§10.17).
AssetType.title: AssetType

ClaimRiskLevel.description:
How much substantiation a claim needs before it is safe to broadcast.

Recorded per claim so the review UI can order the queue by consequence:
an unverified `HIGH` claim about infant safety deserves attention before a
`LOW` one about colour.
ClaimRiskLevel.title: ClaimRiskLevel

ClaimStatus.description:
Whether a claim may be used (§10.8).

§109 is unambiguous: only `VERIFIED` claims reach a script.
ClaimStatus.title: ClaimStatus

ClaimType.description:
What a marketing claim asserts (§10.8).

Not enumerated by the taskbook. The split is by *what would have to be
true* for the claim to be honest, because that is what decides whether it
needs a verified fact behind it (§13, §109).
ClaimType.title: ClaimType

verify.description: Confirm the fact as you create it. Only honoured for facts a user supplied — AI-sourced facts are always AI_INFERRED (§13).
verify.title: Verify

DependencyStatus.description: Result of a single readiness probe.
DependencyStatus.title: DependencyStatus

ErrorCode.description: The complete set of error codes (§65).
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

details.description: Optional structured context. Never contains secrets.
details.title: Details

message.description: Human-readable, safe to display to a user.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Correlates this response with the server logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

ErrorResponse.description: Uniform error envelope returned by every failing endpoint.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FactSourceType.description:
Where a fact came from (§10.7).

Distinct from :class:`VerificationStatus`, which is how much it is
trusted. A fact can be `AI_VISION` in origin and `VERIFIED` in status —
that is precisely the review workflow §13 describes — but the origin is
never overwritten, so "a human confirmed something the AI guessed" stays
distinguishable from "a human typed it in".
FactSourceType.title: FactSourceType

FactType.description:
What kind of thing a product fact asserts (§10.7).

The taskbook names ``fact_type`` without enumerating it. These values are
chosen so that the *risky* categories are separable: §13's forbidden
example ("除甲醛率 99.9%") is a `PERFORMANCE` fact, and being able to
identify that class by type is what lets the claim rules treat it more
strictly than, say, a colour.
FactType.title: FactType

MediaAssetDetailResponse.description: An asset plus a short-lived URL to fetch it (§110).
MediaAssetDetailResponse.title: MediaAssetDetailResponse

MediaAssetResponse.description:
An asset as the client sees it.

Deliberately does **not** expose `bucket` or `object_key`. Those are
infrastructure: revealing them tells a client where files live and invites
code that constructs storage paths instead of asking for a signed URL.
MediaAssetResponse.title: MediaAssetResponse

size_bytes.description: The file's size as the client sees it. Checked again against the stored object at completion — this is an early rejection, not the authoritative limit.
size_bytes.title: Size Bytes

PresignResponse.description: Instructions for the browser's direct-to-storage PUT.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the URL stops working.
expires_in.title: Expires In

headers.description: Headers that must accompany the PUT. They are part of the signature, so omitting or changing one makes storage reject the upload.
headers.title: Headers

upload_url.description: Presigned URL. Send the file body here with PUT.
upload_url.title: Upload Url

PresignResponse.title: PresignResponse

ProductAssetRole.description:
What a product image shows (§10.6).

The role is not decoration: PHASE 8's prompt compiler picks reference
imagery by role, so "the front of the product" has to be answerable
without a human looking at the picture.
ProductAssetRole.title: ProductAssetRole

status.description: Only VERIFIED claims may be used in a generated script (§109).

verification_status.description: Only VERIFIED facts may back a claim or reach a generated script (§13). Anything the AI produced is AI_INFERRED until a person confirms it.

ProductStatus.description:
Where a product sits in its lifecycle (§104).

Transitions are validated by :func:`can_transition_product`; §105 forbids
writing a status by assignment, and the same rule is applied here.
ProductStatus.title: ProductStatus

TokenResponse.description:
Issued credentials.

The refresh token is **not** in this body — it is set as an HttpOnly cookie.
Returning it here would put a long-lived credential somewhere JavaScript
can read it.
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

verify.description: Re-confirm after editing. Without it, changing a value drops the fact back to USER_PROVIDED, because whatever was verified before was a different statement.
verify.title: Verify

UploadConfigResponse.description:
What this deployment accepts.

Served so the file picker and the validator agree by construction. A
hardcoded client-side list drifts from the server's and turns a policy
change into a confusing rejection after the transfer.
UploadConfigResponse.title: UploadConfigResponse

VerificationStatus.description:
How much a fact may be trusted (§10.7, §13).

This is the Truth Layer. Only `VERIFIED` facts may back a claim, and only
`VERIFIED` claims may reach a script (§109). Everything the AI produces
starts at `AI_INFERRED` and can only be promoted by a person.
VerificationStatus.title: VerificationStatus

permissions.description: What the caller may do here. The UI uses this to hide actions; the server enforces it regardless (§40).
permissions.title: Permissions

role.description: The calling user's role in this workspace.
role.title: Role

WorkspaceRole.description:
Membership role (§40).

Ordered from most to least privileged; :func:`role_rank` relies on that
ordering for "at least this role" comparisons.
WorkspaceRole.title: WorkspaceRole

info.description:
HTTP API for AI Product Video Studio.

Long-running AI work (analysis, shot generation, TTS, render, QC) is **never**
performed inside a request. Those endpoints validate, create a `GenerationJob`,
enqueue it and return `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` to poll (taskbook §22).

Every failure returns the same envelope:

```json
{"error": {"code": "PROJECT_NOT_FOUND", "message": "...", "request_id": "..."}}
```

`code` comes from a closed set (§65) and is the field clients should branch on.
info.title: AI Product Video Studio API

get.description:
Describe this API version.

Reports which feature flags are on so a client can adapt without probing
endpoints that are deliberately disabled.

post.description:
Exchange email and password for tokens.

Every failure returns the same error regardless of cause, and the
no-such-user path still performs a password hash, so neither the response
nor its timing reveals whether an email is registered.

Revoke the refresh token and clear the cookie.

Succeeds even without a valid token: a logout that fails leaves the user
believing they are signed out when they are not.

Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access token.

The presented token is revoked as part of the exchange, so a stolen one is
usable at most once.

Register a user and their personal workspace, then sign them in.

A user without a workspace cannot use the product at all, so both are
created in one transaction.

get.description: Every workspace the caller belongs to. Never any others.

schema.title: Response List Workspaces Api V1 Workspaces Get

post.description: Create a workspace. The caller becomes its OWNER.

get.description:
Fetch one workspace.

Returns 404 — not 403 — when the caller is not a member, so workspace ids
cannot be probed for existence across tenants.
Finished assets in this workspace, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Assets Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Assets Get

get.description: One asset, with a short-lived signed URL to fetch its bytes.
get.summary: Get one asset with a download URL

schema.title: Response List Members Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Members Get

post.description:
Add an existing user. Requires `member:invite`.

Granting OWNER additionally requires `member:update_role`, so an admin
cannot escalate by inviting an account they control as an owner.

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the workspace yourself.

Leaving needs no permission; removing someone else requires
`member:remove`. Removing the last owner is refused either way.

patch.description:
Change a role. Requires `member:update_role` (OWNER only).

Demoting the last owner is refused: a workspace with no owner cannot be
billed, deleted, or have its membership managed.

schema.title: Response List Products Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products Get

post.description: Create a product. Always starts in DRAFT (§104).

patch.description:
Edit descriptive fields.

`status` is deliberately not editable here — §105 forbids arbitrary status
writes, so transitions go through their own endpoints.

schema.title: Response List Product Assets Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Assets Get

post.description:
Attach an already-uploaded media asset (§10.6).

The first image attached becomes the primary one automatically.
post.summary: Attach an image to a product

delete.description: Detach an image. The underlying file is untouched (§163 reclaims it).

schema.title: Response List Claims Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Claims Get

post.description: Propose a marketing claim. Always created SUGGESTED (§10.8).

get.description:
§109's `get_verified_claims`, exposed over HTTP.

A separate route rather than a query parameter, so "the claims that may be
broadcast" is a distinct thing a caller asks for rather than a filter it
has to remember to apply.

schema.title: Response List Verified Claims Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Claims Verified Get

post.description:
Approve a claim (§13, §109).

Refused with `CLAIM_NOT_VERIFIED` when the claim asserts something
checkable and cites no verified fact. Only EMOTIONAL claims — which assert
nothing substantiable — are exempt.

schema.title: Response List Facts Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Products  Product Id  Facts Get

post.description:
Record something true about the product (§10.7).

Facts created here are `USER_INPUT`: this endpoint is a person typing.
The analyser's AI-sourced facts go through the same service and are forced
to `AI_INFERRED` (§13) — there is no route that can create a verified AI
fact.

patch.description:
Edit a fact, optionally re-confirming it.

Changing the value withdraws any prior verification and sends claims that
cited it back for review — they were approved against a different
statement.

post.description:
Mark a fact wrong.

Any verified claim that cited it is demoted to SUGGESTED in the same
transaction — evidence withdrawn means the sentence built on it is no
longer approved.

Take responsibility for a fact (§13).

Records who confirmed it and when. This is the only way a fact becomes
usable as evidence.

Move a product to READY.

Refused unless at least one fact has been verified: a product with nothing
confirmed has nothing a script could truthfully say (§13).

get.description: The accepted formats and limits for this deployment.

post.description:
Reserve a key and sign a PUT the browser performs itself.

Creates the asset in `PENDING`. Nothing is served from it until
`complete` has verified the object.

Validate the uploaded object and make the asset usable.

Idempotent: completing an asset that is already `READY` returns it
unchanged, so a retry after a lost response is safe.

get.description: Report that the process is alive. Never touches backing services.

Report whether every backing service is usable.

Returns 503 when any dependency fails so load balancers stop routing here
rather than serving errors to users. Probes run concurrently: three
sequential timeouts would exceed most orchestrators' probe budget.

503.description: One or more dependencies are not ready.
